content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Matthew Mejia (E034) requests write access to Payroll.

There are conflicting notes from HR (Note 1) and Security (Note 2).

Note 1 (HR): role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation write.
Note 2 (Security): employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read.

The access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist role. Matthew is Analyst, so not admin.

The conflict: HR says full_time, Security says contractor. Which to trust? Security DB typically has employment type info too. Security says contractor with basic training.

Given conflicting facts, the safer/conservative approach: Security note says contractor with basic training, meaning max is read. HR says full-time max write. Since we have conflicting info, we should grant the lower maximum? Actually the policy decision: if requested write, and if full-time, write is allowed. If contractor with basic training, max read, so grant read.

The recommendation from Security is read, from HR is write. Since conflicting evidence, prudent to grant the more restrictive level, read. Also, the requested level write is above the max under the security facts (read), so grant the maximum, read.

I'll go with read, based on security DB showing contractor with basic training. Let me submit read.
